newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end sharply up as strike fears ease.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end sharply up as strike fears ease.

text.p: Stocks closed sharply higher on Wednesday as sentiment was buoyed by signs that strikes were fizzling out, brokers said.
Talk that foreign investors are coming back into the market also boosted local investors' confidence, they said.
The composite index, which briefly sank into negative territory due to profit-taking, ended at a provisional 699.76, up 1.92 percent or 13.17 points.
Expectations the U.S. market was due for a sharp retreat this year sparked speculation that foreign funds will turn towards South Korean and other Asian markets, brokers said.
"Foreign buying is increasing on the perception that the market is undervalued and that the economy had reached its bottom," said a Seoul Securities broker.
Despite all-out strike calls by the nation's two main union umbrella bodies, Seoul was largely unaffected by the strikes on Wednesday. Buses and subways ran normally.
South Korean industries have been hurt by strikes that erupted late last year in protest at a new labour law.

Blue chips closed higher, mainly on buying spree sparked by increased foreign buying in these shares. Samsung Electronics was up 1,300 won to 48,800 and Korea Mobile Telecom rose 39,500 won to its daily limit of 536,000.
Bank shares closed lower on profit-taking following last week's rally on speculation that mergers and acquisitions could become active this year in this sector.
Bucking the overall rise, the banking sub-index shed 1.15 percent, or 5.23 points, to 449.70.
March index futures contracts rose 5.2 points to 76.00 while the KOSPI-200 index ended 1.2 points higher at 74.47.
